newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast prods little changed amid subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast prods little changed amid subdued trade.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined products were flat Thursday amid relatively flat futures markets and little trader participation, dealers said.

Crude oil for July delivery on the NYMEX edged up 16 cents a barrel to $18.69 Thursday, the second straight day of modest gains. Refined product futures were also little changed today, with heating oil up 0.10 cents a gallon, and unleaded gasoline up 0.54 cents a gallon
Meanwhile, traders heard rumors that a gasoline-making unit was shut at Shell's refinery near San Francisco, tightening supplies in the area.
The company was not immediately available for comment and prices appeared little changed as a result.
June supplies of Los Angeles cleaner-burning CARB gasoline were bid and offered 1.00 cent a gallon lower Thursday at 54/55 cents, while conventional gasoline was unchanged at 53/54 cents.
CARB diesel in Los Angeles was steady at 56/58 cents, traders said.
Reformulated gasoline in L.A. and San Francisco was offered at a one cent discount to L.A. CARB gasoline.
